results.title: Tensor inverses are unique up to isomorphism in braided categories
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a braided monoidal category, tensoring with the unit is cancellative up to isomorphism: if `M ⊗ N ≅ 𝟙`, `M' ⊗ N' ≅ 𝟙`, and `M ≅ M'`, then `N ≅ N'`.

part.title: Point stabilizers of infinite doubly transitive groups

path: Point stabilizers of infinite doubly transitive groups

results.title: Doubly transitive group with infinite cyclic point stabilizer (Kourovka 10.63)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there exist a group $G$ and a faithful action of $G$ on a set $X$ such that for any two ordered pairs of distinct points of $X$ some element of $G$ maps the first to the second, and the stabilizer of some point $x \in X$ is isomorphic to the infinite cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: No doubly transitive group has an infinite cyclic point stabilizer (Kourovka 10.63)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a group $G$ acts faithfully on a set $X$ such that for any two ordered pairs of distinct points of $X$ some element of $G$ maps the first to the second, then no point stabilizer of the action is isomorphic to the infinite cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Non-periodic doubly transitive group with periodic point stabilizer (Kourovka 10.64)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there exist a group $G$ and a faithful action of $G$ on a set $X$ such that for any two ordered pairs of distinct points of $X$ some element of $G$ maps the first to the second, $G$ has an element of infinite order, and every element of the stabilizer of some point $x \in X$ has finite order.

results.title: A non-periodic doubly transitive group with a periodic point stabilizer (Kourovka 10.64)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a group $G$ with an element of infinite order and a faithful action of $G$ on a set $X$ such that for any two ordered pairs of distinct points of $X$ some element of $G$ maps the first to the second, and every element of the stabilizer of some point $x \in X$ has finite order.

results.title: Polynomials in two complex variables
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A plane polynomial is a polynomial $f \in \mathbb{C}[X_0, X_1]$ in two variables $X_0, X_1$ with complex coefficients.

results.title: Points of the complex affine plane
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A point of the complex affine plane is a pair $a = (a_0, a_1)$ of complex numbers, that is, an element of $\mathbb{C}^2$, with coordinates indexed by $0$ and $1$.

results.title: Translate of a plane polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a polynomial $f \in \mathbb{C}[x_1, x_2]$ and a point $a = (a_1, a_2) \in \mathbb{C}^2$, the translate of $f$ by $a$ is the polynomial $f(x_1 + a_1, x_2 + a_2)$, obtained by substituting $x_i + a_i$ for $x_i$. It moves the point $a$ to the origin.

results.title: Total degree of a monomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The total degree of the exponent vector $m = (m_0, m_1)$ of a monomial $X_0^{m_0} X_1^{m_1}$ in two variables is $m_0 + m_1$.

results.title: Multiplicity of a plane polynomial at a point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a polynomial $f \in \mathbb{C}[X_0, X_1]$ and a point $a = (a_0, a_1) \in \mathbb{C}^2$, the multiplicity of $f$ at $a$ is the least total degree of a monomial occurring with nonzero coefficient in the translated polynomial $f(X_0 + a_0, X_1 + a_1)$. For the zero polynomial it is $0$.

results.title: The first-coordinate line through a point has multiplicity one there
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every point $a = (a_0, a_1) \in \mathbb{C}^2$, the polynomial $X_0 - a_0 \in \mathbb{C}[X_0, X_1]$, which defines the line through $a$ on which the first coordinate is constant, has multiplicity $1$ at $a$.

results.title: Seshadri ratios of ten points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a configuration $x = (x_0, \dots, x_9)$ of ten points of $\mathbb{C}^2$, not necessarily distinct, the Seshadri ratios of $x$ are the real numbers $\deg f / \sum_{i=0}^{9} \operatorname{mult}_{x_i} f$, where $f$ ranges over the nonzero polynomials in $\mathbb{C}[X_0, X_1]$ with $\sum_{i=0}^{9} \operatorname{mult}_{x_i} f > 0$, $\deg f$ is the total degree of $f$, and $\operatorname{mult}_{x_i} f$ is the…

results.title: Seshadri constant of ten affine points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a configuration $x = (x_0, \dots, x_9)$ of ten points of $\mathbb{C}^2$, not necessarily distinct, the affine Seshadri constant of $x$ is the infimum of the ratios $\deg f / \sum_{i=0}^{9} \operatorname{mult}_{x_i} f$ over all nonzero polynomials $f \in \mathbb{C}[X_0, X_1]$ with $\sum_{i=0}^{9} \operatorname{mult}_{x_i} f > 0$, where $\deg f$ is the total degree of $f$ and $\operatorname{mult}_{x_i} f$ is the…

results.title: The affine Seshadri constant is at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every configuration $x = (x_0, \dots, x_9)$ of ten points of $\mathbb{C}^2$, not necessarily distinct, the affine Seshadri constant of $x$ is at most $1$.

results.title: Generic ten-point Seshadri constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The generic ten-point Seshadri constant is the supremum, over all configurations $x = (x_0, \dots, x_9)$ of ten pairwise distinct points of $\mathbb{C}^2$, of the affine Seshadri constant of $x$.

results.title: Ten-point Seshadri constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The ten-point Seshadri constant is the generic ten-point Seshadri constant: the supremum, over all configurations of ten pairwise distinct points of $\mathbb{C}^2$, of their affine Seshadri constants.

results.title: Nagata's conjecture for ten points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that the generic ten-point Seshadri constant of $\mathbb{P}^2$, in the affine-chart model, equals $1/\sqrt{10}$.

results.title: Eckl's 2008 lower bound for the ten-point Seshadri constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The generic ten-point Seshadri constant of $\mathbb{P}^2$, in the affine-chart model, is at least $4/13$.

results.title: Harbourne–Roé lower bound for the ten-point Seshadri constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The generic ten-point Seshadri constant of $\mathbb{P}^2$, in the affine-chart model, is at least $177/560$.

results.title: Ciliberto–Miranda lower bound for the ten-point Seshadri constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The generic ten-point Seshadri constant of $\mathbb{P}^2$, in the affine-chart model, is at least $55/174$.

results.title: Eckl's 2011 lower bound for the ten-point Seshadri constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The generic ten-point Seshadri constant of $\mathbb{P}^2$, in the affine-chart model, is at least $117/370$.

results.title: Submaximal upper bound for the ten-point Seshadri constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The generic ten-point Seshadri constant of $\mathbb{P}^2$, in the affine-chart model, is at most $1/\sqrt{10}$.

results.title: Coordinate functional of a basis as a continuous linear map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The `i`-th coordinate functional of a basis, as a continuous linear map. In finite dimensions every linear map is continuous, so this is just the coordinate functional bundled with its continuity.

results.title: Operator norm of a norm-bounded coordinate functional is at most 1
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the `i`-th coordinate functional is bounded by the norm, its operator norm is at most `1`.

results.title: Coordinate functional of a unit basis vector has operator norm 1
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the `i`-th basis vector has norm `1` and the `i`-th coordinate functional is bounded by the norm, its operator norm is exactly `1`: it attains `1` at the `i`-th basis vector.

results.title: Auerbach basis
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An *Auerbach basis* is a basis of unit vectors whose coordinate functionals all have operator norm `1`.

results.title: Auerbach's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite-dimensional normed space over `𝕜` has an Auerbach basis, indexed by `Fin (Module.finrank 𝕜 E)`.

results.title: Weak convergence of probability measures on configuration space
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Weak convergence of a sequence of probability measures on `ConfigSpace E`: convergence in the topology of `ProbabilityMeasure (ConfigSpace E)`, whose open sets are generated by the integrals of bounded continuous functions.

results.title: Weak convergence implies convergence of integrals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under weak convergence, the integral of every bounded continuous function converges.

results.title: Convergence of integrals implies weak convergence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the integral of every bounded continuous function converges, the measures converge weakly.

results.title: Cylinder events are clopen
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A cylinder event of `ConfigSpace E`, determined by finitely many coordinates, is clopen.

results.title: Portmanteau theorem for clopen events
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under weak convergence on `ConfigSpace E`, the probability of every clopen event converges (portmanteau theorem).

results.title: Increasing-event probabilities along an increasing chain are monotone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Along a chain `μ₀ ≼ μ₁ ≼ ⋯`, the probability of an increasing event is monotone.

results.title: Increasing-event probabilities along a decreasing chain are antitone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Along a chain `⋯ ≼ μ₁ ≼ μ₀`, the probability of an increasing event is antitone.

results.title: Weak limit of an increasing chain dominates its terms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The weak limit of an increasing chain gives each increasing clopen event at least the probability any term of the chain gives it.

results.title: Weak limit of a decreasing chain is dominated by its terms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The weak limit of a decreasing chain gives each increasing clopen event at most the probability any term of the chain gives it.

results.title: Lower bounds on clopen-event probabilities pass to weak limits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A lower bound on the probabilities of a clopen event along a weakly convergent sequence passes to the limit.

results.title: Upper bounds on clopen-event probabilities pass to weak limits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An upper bound on the probabilities of a clopen event along a weakly convergent sequence passes to the limit.

results.title: Stochastic domination from below passes to weak limits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `ρ ≼ μₙ` for all `n` and `μₙ → ν` weakly, then `ρ(A) ≤ ν(A)` for every increasing clopen event `A`.

results.title: Stochastic domination from above passes to weak limits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `μₙ ≼ ρ` for all `n` and `μₙ → ν` weakly, then `ν(A) ≤ ρ(A)` for every increasing clopen event `A`.

results.title: Probability measures agreeing on clopen sets are equal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two probability measures on `ConfigSpace E` that agree on clopen sets are equal: the clopen cylinder events form a generating π-system.

results.title: Subsequential weak limits are determined by clopen-event limits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the probabilities of clopen events converge to `L`, every subsequential weak limit `ξ` satisfies `ξ(A) = L(A)` on clopen `A`.

results.title: Convergence on clopen events implies weak convergence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the probability of every clopen event converges along a sequence of probability measures on `ConfigSpace E`, the sequence converges weakly: all subsequential limits (which exist by Prokhorov) agree on clopen sets, hence coincide.

results.title: Convergence of increasing-event probabilities along an increasing chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Along a chain `μ₀ ≼ μ₁ ≼ ⋯`, the probability of an increasing clopen event converges to its supremum.

results.title: Erdős Problem 484: linearly many monochromatic sums
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: This is the statement that there is a real constant $c > 0$ such that for every integer $k \ge 1$ there is an $N_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ with the following property: for every $N \ge N_0$ and every colouring $f : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, \dots, k-1\}$, at least $cN$ of the integers $n \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ can be written as $n = a + b$ with $a, b \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, $a \ne b$ and $f(a) = f(b)$.

results.title: Erdős–Sárközy–Sós theorem on monochromatic sums (Erdős Problem 484)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a real constant $c > 0$ such that for every integer $k \ge 1$ there is an $N_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $N \ge N_0$ and every colouring $f : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, \dots, k-1\}$, at least $cN$ of the integers $n \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ can be written as $n = a + b$ with $a, b \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, $a \ne b$ and $f(a) = f(b)$.

results.title: Starting positions of Kolakoski blocks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $K_1, K_2, K_3, \ldots$ of natural numbers, the starting positions $s_n$ of its blocks are defined by $s_1 = 1$ and $s_{n+1} = s_n + K_n$ for every $n \ge 1$, together with the convention $s_0 = 0$.

results.title: Kolakoski sequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sequence $K_1, K_2, K_3, \ldots$ of natural numbers is a Kolakoski sequence when $K_1 = 1$, every $K_n$ with $n \ge 1$ is $1$ or $2$, and $K$ describes its own runs in the following sense. Let $s_1 = 1$ and $s_{n+1} = s_n + K_n$ for $n \ge 1$, and call block $n$ the set of positions $i$ with $s_n \le i < s_n + K_n$. For every $n \ge 1$, every term $K_i$ with $i$ in block $n$ equals $1$ if $n$ is odd and $2$ if…

results.title: Hypercube graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_n$ is the simple graph whose vertices are the functions from $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to the Booleans $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$, with an edge between two vertices exactly when they differ in exactly one coordinate.

results.title: Adjacency in the hypercube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and all vertices $x, y$ of the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_n$ (functions from $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to the Booleans), $x$ and $y$ are adjacent in $Q_n$ if and only if there is exactly one coordinate $i$ with $x_i \ne y_i$.

results.title: No two vertices of the zero-dimensional hypercube are adjacent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all vertices $x, y$ of the $0$-dimensional hypercube $Q_0$, $x$ and $y$ are not adjacent in $Q_0$.

results.title: An edge of the one-dimensional hypercube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the $1$-dimensional hypercube $Q_1$, the constant vertex $\mathrm{true}$ and the constant vertex $\mathrm{false}$ are adjacent.

results.title: The zero-dimensional hypercube has no edges
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The edge set of the $0$-dimensional hypercube $Q_0$ is empty.

results.title: Subgraphs of the hypercube have at most as many edges
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, every subgraph of the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_n$ has at most as many edges as $Q_n$.

results.title: Hypercube Turán number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a simple graph $H$, let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube. The hypercube Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(Q_n, H)$ is the largest number of edges of a subgraph (not necessarily spanning) of $Q_n$ that contains no copy of $H$, that is, no subgraph isomorphic to $H$; it is $0$ when no such subgraph exists.

results.title: The hypercube Turán number bounds every free subgraph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every simple graph $H$, let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube and let $\mathrm{ex}(Q_n, H)$ be the hypercube Turán number of $H$ in $Q_n$. If $S$ is a subgraph of $Q_n$ that contains no copy of $H$, then $S$ has at most $\mathrm{ex}(Q_n, H)$ edges.

results.title: Upper bound for the hypercube Turán number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every simple graph $H$, writing $Q_n$ for the $n$-dimensional hypercube, the hypercube Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(Q_n, H)$ is at most the number of edges of $Q_n$.

results.title: Attainment of the hypercube Turán number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $H$ a simple graph, $Q_n$ the $n$-dimensional hypercube, and $\mathrm{ex}(Q_n, H)$ the hypercube Turán number. If $Q_n$ has at least one subgraph (not necessarily spanning) that contains no copy of $H$, then some subgraph $S$ of $Q_n$ contains no copy of $H$ and has exactly $\mathrm{ex}(Q_n, H)$ edges.

results.title: The hypercube Turán number in dimension zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every simple graph $H$, writing $Q_0$ for the $0$-dimensional hypercube, the hypercube Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(Q_0, H)$ is $0$.

results.title: Four-cycle-free subgraphs of the hypercubes of dimensions one to six
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, let $C_4$ be the cycle on four vertices, and let $\mathrm{ex}(Q_n, C_4)$ be the largest number of edges of a subgraph of $Q_n$ that contains no copy of $C_4$. Then for $n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$ the value of $\mathrm{ex}(Q_n, C_4)$ is $1$, $3$, $9$, $24$, $56$ and $132$ respectively.

results.title: Lower bound for four-cycle-free subgraphs of the seven-dimensional hypercube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $Q_7$ be the $7$-dimensional hypercube and $C_4$ the cycle on four vertices. The largest number $\mathrm{ex}(Q_7, C_4)$ of edges of a subgraph of $Q_7$ that contains no copy of $C_4$ is at least $304$.

results.title: Upper bound for four-cycle-free subgraphs of the seven-dimensional hypercube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $Q_7$ be the $7$-dimensional hypercube and $C_4$ the cycle on four vertices. The largest number $\mathrm{ex}(Q_7, C_4)$ of edges of a subgraph of $Q_7$ that contains no copy of $C_4$ is at most $308$.

results.title: Lower bound for four-cycle-free subgraphs of the eight-dimensional hypercube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $Q_8$ be the $8$-dimensional hypercube and $C_4$ the cycle on four vertices. The largest number $\mathrm{ex}(Q_8, C_4)$ of edges of a subgraph of $Q_8$ that contains no copy of $C_4$ is at least $682$.
